title: Idempotency Keys in Distributed Systems: Preventing Duplicate Transactions
concept: How payment gateways and distributed APIs use unique idempotency keys stored in Redis or transactional databases with atomic conditional writes (SETNX) to achieve exactly-once processing semantics over at-least-once network delivery.

title: The Saga Pattern: Orchestration vs Choreography in Distributed Transactions
concept: Managing distributed transactions without two-phase commit (2PC) using compensating actions, contrasting central workflow orchestrators with decentralized event choreography via Kafka and RabbitMQ.

title: Cache-Aside & Thundering Herd: Defending Distributed Caches at Scale
concept: Mitigating cache stampedes, hotkey contention, and dog-piling effects during TTL expiration using probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm), mutex locks, and read-through caching patterns.

title: Consistent Hashing & Database Sharding: Dynamic Node Scaling
concept: Partitioning massive relational and NoSQL databases horizontally with consistent hashing rings and virtual nodes, minimizing key re-distribution when cluster nodes join or leave.

title: Distributed Rate Limiting: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Sliding Window Counter
concept: Architecting high-throughput API rate limiters using Redis sliding window logs and memory-efficient Lua scripts to enforce client quotas without race conditions.

title: CQRS and Event Sourcing: High Performance Read-Write Segregation
concept: Decoupling command mutations from query models to enable hyper-optimized read projections, eventual consistency handling, and full auditability through immutable event logs.

title: Circuit Breakers & Bulkhead Isolation: Building Fault-Tolerant Microservices
concept: Preventing cascading failures in distributed call chains using three-state circuit breakers (Closed, Open, Half-Open), thread-pool isolation bulkheads, and exponential backoff with jitter.

title: Distributed Locks with Redis Redlock: Guarantees, Caveats, and Fencing Tokens
concept: Deep dive into Martin Kleppmann's critique of Redlock, the hazards of GC pauses and clock skew, and why monotonically increasing fencing tokens are mandatory for data safety.

title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters): Future-Proof Core Business Logic
concept: Isolating domain entities and use cases from database drivers, external transport layers, and framework dependencies using inversion of control and explicit port interfaces.

title: Consensus Protocols: Why Raft and Paxos Outperform 2PC in Modern Clouds
concept: Examining why traditional Two-Phase Commit is blocking and fragile during network partitions, and how quorum-based consensus (Raft/Paxos) provides high availability and partition tolerance.

title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP): Beyond Mere Dependency Injection
concept: Distinguishing DIP from DI containers: creating stable abstractions owned by the high-level policy rather than low-level detail modules to eliminate circular coupling.

title: Vector Clocks and Version Vectors: Resolving Concurrent Writes in AP Databases
concept: Detecting causal concurrency and conflicting writes in Dynamo-style distributed stores (Cassandra, Riak) using vector clocks and application-level CRDT reconciliation.

title: Strangler Fig Pattern: Safely Deconstructing the Monolith Without Big Bangs
concept: Incrementally replacing legacy monolithic endpoints with modern microservices via reverse-proxy traffic routing, feature flags, and shadow traffic validation.

title: Worker Pools and Backpressure: Preventing Node.js Event Loop Starvation
concept: Managing heavy I/O and CPU workloads using bounded queue worker pools, stream backpressure, and graceful degradation under sudden burst traffic spikes.

title: Aggregate Roots in Domain-Driven Design: Enforcing Transactional Invariants
concept: Designing transactional boundaries around entity clusters, preventing direct external access to child entities, and ensuring consistency boundaries remain atomic and lean.

title: B-Trees vs LSM-Trees: Storage Engine Tradeoffs for Read vs Write-Heavy Workloads
concept: Contrasting MySQL/Postgres in-place B+Tree indexing with RocksDB/Cassandra append-only Log-Structured Merge trees, write amplification, and compaction strategies.

title: Expand and Contract Pattern: Zero-Downtime Database Schema Migrations
concept: Safely altering production tables with hundreds of millions of records using phased additive column expansion, dual-writing, backfilling, and contract deprecation.

title: Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry: Context Propagation Across Microservices
concept: Propagating W3C TraceContext headers (traceparent) across async queues and HTTP boundaries to trace cross-service latency bottlenecks and isolate failure cascades.
